svg.title: Reset vs. Revert
svg.desc: Animation comparing git reset --hard HEAD~1 and git revert HEAD for an already-pushed commit C: reset removes C locally, the push is rejected and forcing it rewrites shared history; revert adds commit R that undoes C and a normal push works.

g.text: $ git push --force → C erased on origin
teammates who pulled C now have broken history
R = the exact inverse of C
teammates just git pull — nothing breaks
Same goal — undo commit C, which is already pushed. Two very different results.
reset moves your branch back: C disappears from your history…
…so the push is rejected. Forcing it rewrites history your team already has.
revert adds R, the inverse of C. History stays intact; a normal push works.
Rule: reset only local, unpushed commits. Revert anything that's shared.
